hero.title: File:StateLibQld 1 258434 Hand coloured photograph of the Queen Cross Reef gold mine, Charters Towers, 1904.jpg
hero.credit: Item is held by John Oxley Library, State Library of Queensland.
hero.source: StateLibQld 1 258434 Hand coloured photograph of the Queen Cross Reef gold mine, Charters Towers, 1904
hero.description:
Hand coloured photograph of the Queen Cross Reef gold mine, Charters Towers, 1904.
Due to the Gold boom between 1872 and 1899, Charters Towers operated the only Stock Exchange outside of a capital city. During this period, the population was approximately 27,000, making Charters Towers, Queensland s largest City outside of Brisbane. Today the main industries are mining and beef cattle. There are also several world class boarding schools in the area.

This is a photograph taken from a small album of hand coloured photographs about Charters Towers, including some mines, published by T. Willmett & Son, Charters Towers in 1904.
categories: Images from the State Library of Queensland

gallery.filename: StateLibQld 1 255715 Battery for No. 2 Queen Mine, Charters Towers, ca. 1890.jpg
gallery.title: File:StateLibQld 1 255715 Battery for No. 2 Queen Mine, Charters Towers, ca. 1890.jpg
gallery.description:
Battery for No. 2 Queen Mine, Charters Towers, ca. 1890.
Due to the gold mining boom between 1872 and 1899, Charters Towers operated the only Stock Exchange outside of a capital city. During this period, the population was approximately 27,000, making Charters Towers Queensland's largest city outside of Brisbane. The decline of mining following World War I saw the population shrink and the town become the supply centre of the Dalrymple Shire as well as the educational centre for students from all over North Queensland.
